stories.title: Building Collapse in Gaza City Results in Multiple Fatalities and Missing Persons
stories.summary: A multi-storey building in Gaza City collapsed, leading to at least 12 to 21 confirmed deaths, including children, and dozens of individuals reported missing. The building housed displaced families and had suffered damage from previous Israeli strikes. Rescue operations are ongoing, but efforts are hindered by restrictions on heavy machinery in the area.

stories.title: EU Proposes Canada as First Associate Member Amid Strengthening Ties
stories.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed that Canada become the European Union's first 'associate member,' a status not currently defined in EU treaties. This announcement was made during her annual State of the Union address, where she highlighted shared democratic values and common interests between the EU and Canada. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, present at the event, expressed interest in forming a unique alliance with the EU without seeking full membership.

stories.title: Kennedy Center Board Votes to Close Amid Legal Dispute Over Trump's Name
stories.summary: The Kennedy Center board voted to temporarily close the performing arts center, citing financial issues and the need for renovations. This decision followed a federal judge's ruling that blocked the board from adding President Trump's name to the building or grounds. The closure comes amid tensions, as Trump threatened to cancel a significant renovation project if his name was not reinstated.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia Claims Houthi Drone Targeted Mecca, Warns of Consequences
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has accused Yemen's Houthi rebels of attempting to attack Mecca, Islam's holiest city, claiming its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a drone deployed by the Houthis. The Saudi-led coalition emphasized that the security of Mecca is a 'red line' and warned of potential deterrent measures. In response, the Houthis have denied the allegations, labeling them as false.

stories.title: Former Kosovo President Thaci Convicted of War Crimes and Sentenced to 25 Years
stories.summary: Hashim Thaci, the former President of Kosovo, has been convicted of war crimes by a tribunal in The Hague and sentenced to 25 years in prison. The court found him guilty of crimes committed during Kosovo's war for independence from Serbia, including murder, torture, and illegal arrests. The verdict has elicited strong reactions among the people of Kosovo.

stories.title: Renewed Violence in Yemen Displaces Thousands Amid Ceasefire Collapse
stories.summary: A surge in violence in Yemen has led to the end of a ceasefire and the displacement of approximately 125,000 people in the past two weeks. Many are fleeing to makeshift camps, such as Al Kadha in Taiz, as fighting intensifies in the region. The situation has resulted in overcrowded camps and a humanitarian crisis.

stories.summary: All four supporting acts for Ed Sheeran's US tour have withdrawn in solidarity with rapper Macklemore, who was dropped from the tour after making comments in support of Palestine. They announced their decision on social media, highlighting their support for Macklemore amidst the controversy surrounding his remarks about Gaza.
